370758.title: LQYZ's non-Schur-positivity conjecture for products of chains
370758.statement: Let $\textbf m$ and $\textbf n$ denote chains indexed by the positive integers $m$ and $n$, and let $\textbf m\times\textbf n$ be their product lattice. A lattice is **Schur positive** when the chromatic symmetric function of its incomparability graph is Schur positive. **LQYZ's conjecture.** For any positive integer pair $(m,n)$ such that $m\ge 8$ and $n\ge 2$, or that $m\ge n+5$ and $n\ge 3$, the lattice $\textbf m\times\textbf n$ is not Schur positive. This extends a known theorem for a subfamily of products of chains and predicts the full non-Schur-positive range described in the conjecture. The supplied text gives no resolution, so the conjecture remains open.

370775.title: Bremner's conjecture on additive rigidity of elliptic-curve points
370775.statement:
Let $E/\a0\mathbb{Q}$ be an elliptic curve of Mordell\a0\a0Weil rank $r$, and let $\{P_1,\ldots,P_N\}$ be a sequence of rational points whose $x$-coordinates form an arithmetic progression in $\mathbb{Q}$. **Bremner's conjecture.** There exists an absolute constant $A$ such that

$$
N \ll A^r.
$$

This precise formulation expresses the idea that long $x$-arithmetic progressions should force large Mordell\a0\a0Weil rank. It is supported by several results, and Garcia-Fritz and Pasten proved it for families with fixed $j$-invariant; the general conjecture remains open.

370778.title: Non-concavity conjecture for the critical curve of long-range percolation
370778.statement:
Let $d\geq 2$, let $k>1$, and consider the critical curve $p\mapsto q_c(p)$ for the case $m=2$ and $l=1$ of long-range percolation on an oriented $d$-ary tree. For a function $q_c$, concavity on an interval means that its graph lies above every chord joining two points of the graph.

**Non-concavity conjecture.** There exists $\delta=\delta(k,d)>0$ such that $p\mapsto q_c(p)$ is not concave on $[0,\delta]$.

This claim formalizes the observation that the critical curve, contrary to an intuitive concave depiction, appears convex near $p=0$ when $l=1$ and $k\geq 2$. The supplied text does not state whether the claim has been proved or remains open.

371042.title: Embedding conjecture for three-dimensional symmetric designs from regular Hadamard matrices
371042.statement:
Let $H$) be a regular Hadamard matrix of order $v^2$. A **three-dimensional embedding conjecture** asserts that there exists a $\mathcal{C}^3_3(v^6,v^8(v^4-1)/2,v^8(v^4-2)/4)$-cube containing a $\mathcal{C}^3_3(v^3,v^4(v^2-1)/2,v^4(v^2-2)/4)$-subcube.

**Embedding conjecture.** If $H$ is a regular Hadamard matrix of order $v^2$, then such a containing cube and subcube exist.

The existence would follow from the cited theorem if $H$ could be embedded in a regular Hadamard matrix of order $v^4$; the authors note that they are unaware of results on embedding regular Hadamard matrices.

371077.title: The Tree Unimodality Conjecture
371077.statement:
Let $T$ be a tree, let $\alpha=\alpha(T)$ be its independence number, and let $a_i$ denote the number of independent sets of cardinality $i$, so that $a_0=1$. **The Tree Unimodality Conjecture.** There exists an index $m$ such that

$$
a_0\leq a_1\leq\cdots\leq a_m\geq a_{m+1}\geq\cdots\geq a_\alpha.
$$

This conjecture asserts unimodality for independence sequences of trees, a family for which unimodality remains a central question despite counterexamples for general graphs. The supplied text does not state whether it has been resolved.

371098.title: The wheel-free Burling-control conjecture
371098.statement: A **wheel** is a graph consisting of an induced cycle of length at least $4$ and one additional vertex adjacent to at least three vertices on the cycle. A graph class is **Burling-controlled** in the sense defined in the source. **Wheel-free Burling-control conjecture.** The class of graphs with no induced wheel is Burling-controlled. This is proposed after Burling graphs refuted wheel-free chi-boundedness; it remains open in the supplied source.

371137.title: Archdeacon's 5-oriented-cycle-double-cover conjecture
371137.statement:
An **oriented $k$-cycle double-cover** (or $k$-OCDC) of a graph is a multiset of $k$ oriented cycles in which every edge occurs in each orientation in exactly one cycle.

**Archdeacon's conjecture.** Every bridgeless graph has a $5$-OCDC.

The conjecture is part of the cycle-double-cover approach to nowhere-zero flow problems. The supplied text states that it is not known whether every bridgeless graph has a $k$-OCDC for some $k$, so this specific assertion remains open.

371226.title: Combinatorial dga model conjecture for surface categories
371226.statement: Let $(S,n,{\bf a})$ be a parametrized surface and let $R(S,n,{\bf a};k)$ be the dga generated by diagrams of $k$ strands between the corresponding collections of arcs. Let $\mu_m$ denote the higher $A_{\infty}$-operations for the associated surface category. **Surface dga model conjecture.** The operations $\mu_m$ are trivial for $m\geq 3$, the resulting structure is isomorphic to $R(S,n,{\bf a};k)$, and the quasi-isomorphism class of $R(S,n,{\bf a};k)$ is independent of the choice of parametrization ${\bf a}$ of $S$. These conjectures would provide a combinatorial description of the partially wrapped $A_{\infty}$-algebras from the geometric construction; the paper presents them as conjectural and gives partial justification.

371234.title: Bollobás–Scott weighted long-cycle conjecture for Eulerian digraphs
371234.statement:
A **digraph** is a directed graph; it is **Eulerian** when it is strongly connected and every vertex has equal in-degree and out-degree. For a digraph $G$, let $A(G)$ denote its arc set, let $w:A(G)\to\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ be a weight function, and write $w(G)$ for the total weight of its arcs. **Bollobás–Scott's weighted long-cycle conjecture.** Every $n$-vertex Eulerian digraph $G$ with a weight function $w:A(G)\to\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ has a directed cycle of length at least

$$
c\cdot\frac{w(G)}{n}
$$

for some universal constant $c>0$. This conjecture proposes a linear lower bound in the average arc weight for the length of a directed cycle and generalizes unweighted long-cycle questions for Eulerian digraphs.

371235.title: Bollobás–Scott linear long-cycle conjecture for Eulerian digraphs
371235.statement:
A **digraph** is Eulerian when it is strongly connected and every vertex has equal in-degree and out-degree. Its average out-degree is the average of the out-degrees of its vertices; denote this quantity by $d$. **Bollobás–Scott's linear long-cycle conjecture.** Every Eulerian digraph with average out-degree $d$ has a directed cycle of length at least

$$
cd
$$

for some universal constant $c>0$. This is a weaker unweighted version of the weighted Bollobás–Scott conjecture and was proposed as an intermediate step toward resolving it; the source does not state a resolution.

371239.title: The Gowers norm additive uncertainty conjecture
371239.statement:
Let $N,d$ be positive integers, let $f:\mathbb{Z}_N^d\to\mathbb{C}$ be a signal with support $E$ and Fourier support $\Sigma$, and let $\|\cdot\|_{U^k}$ denote the Gowers $U^k$ norm for $k\geq 2$. **Gowers norm additive uncertainty conjecture.** One should have

$$
1\leq |E|\cdot\|1_\Sigma\|_{U^k}^{2^k/(k+1)}.
$$
This extends the additive energy uncertainty principle from the $U^2$ norm to higher Gowers norms. The source presents it as a direction for future research and gives no resolution.

371321.title: Generalized asymmetric three-colour Ramsey conjecture
371321.statement:
Let $k$ and $\ell$ be integers with $k \geq \ell \geq 2$. For graphs $G$ and positive integers $a_1,\dots,a_r$, write $G \rightarrow (K_{a_1},\dots,K_{a_r})$ if every $r$-colouring of the edges of $G$ contains a monochromatic copy of $K_{a_i}$ in some colour $i$; write $G \not\rightarrow (K_{a_1},\dots,K_{a_r})$ otherwise.

**Generalized asymmetric three-colour Ramsey conjecture.** For any integers $k \geq \ell \geq 2$, there exists a graph $G$ such that $G \not\rightarrow (K_k,K_k,K_{\ell})$, but $G \rightarrow (K_{k+1},K_{k-1},K_{\ell})$.

This conjecture is presented as a three-colour analogue related to the preceding conjecture in the same way that the preceding two-colour theorem relates to the Nešetřil–Rödl result. Its status is not resolved in the supplied text.

371344.title: Prime-diagonal rank conjecture for graphical Hermite simplices
371344.statement:
Let $G$ be the topological ordering of a graph on $[n]$, and let $B$ be the matrix over ${\mathbb{Z}}/p{\mathbb{Z}}$ given by

$$
B=\sum_{(i,j)\in G}E_{i,j}.
$$

Let $r_p$ be the rank of $B$ over ${\mathbb{Z}}/p{\mathbb{Z}}$, and let $\alpha_i$ be the elementary divisors of $A_{\vec p,G}$. **Prime-diagonal rank conjecture.** The elementary divisors satisfy $\alpha_{r_p}=1$ and $\alpha_{r_p+1}>1$.

This conjecture makes precise the experimental observation that, for a prime diagonal, the rank of the adjacency matrix over ${\mathbb{Z}}/p{\mathbb{Z}}$ determines how powers of $p$ are distributed among the nonunit elementary divisors, extending the preceding result from bipartite graphs to all graphs. Its status is not established in the supplied text.

371394.title: EISPN conjectures for Cartesian products of paths
371394.statement:
Let $P_m$ denote the path of order $m$, and let $\Box$ denote the Cartesian graph product. For a graph $G$, let $EISPN(G)$ denote its efficient isolated private-neighborhood number.

**EISPN path-product conjectures.** If $k \ge 1$, then

$$
EISPN(P_3 \mathbin{\Box} P_{2k})=6k.
$$

If $m \ge 2$, then

$$
EISPN(P_4 \mathbin{\Box} P_m)=4m.
$$

These conjectures are posed from data for graph classes. The source gives no resolution; the first EISPN assertion is presented as an additional conjecture following the EIPN grid conjecture.

371489.title: Ji's length-spectrum rigidity conjecture for rational maps
371489.statement:
Let $f$ and $g$ be non-Lattès rational maps of degree $d\geq 2$. For each $n\geq 1$, let $L_n(f)$ denote the unordered collection of absolute derivatives at the fixed points of $f^n$, and let the length spectrum be the sequence $(L_n(f))_{n\geq 1}$. Let $\tau_d(f)$ denote the multiplier-spectrum invariant introduced in the source, and let $\overline g$ be the complex conjugate of $g$.

**Length-spectrum rigidity conjecture.** If $f$ and $g$ have the same length spectrum, then

$$
\tau_d(f)=\tau_d(g)\quad\text{or}\quad \tau_d(f)=\tau_d(\overline g).
$$

The conjecture gives a precise description of rational maps with identical length spectra. It is presented as a conjecture proposed by Ji and the author; no resolution is supplied in the passage.

371490.title: Ji's multiplier-spectrum injectivity conjecture
371490.statement:
Let $f$ and $g$ be rational maps of degree $d\geq 2$ whose conjugacy classes are different. Let $\tau_d$ be the multiplier-spectrum map, and call two rational maps **elementarily equivalent** in the sense used in the source. A **Lattès map** is a rational map belonging to the Lattès class.

**Multiplier-spectrum injectivity conjecture.** If $\tau_d(f)=\tau_d(g)$, then either

1. $f$ and $g$ are Lattès maps; or
2. $f$ is elementarily equivalent to $g$.

This conjecture asserts that Lattès maps and elementary equivalence are the only obstructions to injectivity of the multiplier spectrum. It is attributed in the passage to Ji and the author, following a question of Pakovich; no resolution is supplied.

371570.title: Full-range low-degree vertex conjecture for intersecting hypergraphs
371570.statement:
Let $[n]=\{1,2,\ldots,n\}$, and let $\mathcal{F}\subset \binom{[n]}{k}$ be an **intersecting family**, meaning that any two members of $\mathcal{F}$ intersect. The degree of a vertex is the number of members of $\mathcal{F}$ containing it.

**Full-range low-degree vertex conjecture.** If $n>2k$, then at least $n-2k$ vertices have degree at most

$$
\binom{n-2}{k-2}.
$$

The paper proves this conclusion under the stronger hypothesis $n\geq 6k$, while the Huang–Zhao theorem gives one such vertex for $n>2k$. The conjecture asks whether the bound of $n-2k$ vertices holds throughout the full range $n>2k$.

371606.title: Irreducibility of extremal synchronizing automata
371606.statement:
Let $\mathcal{A}=(Q,\Sigma,\delta)$ be a synchronizing automaton with $n=|Q|$. Its rank is the cardinality of the image of the state set under a word, and it is **extremal** if its shortest reset word has length exactly $(n-1)^2$. An automaton is **irreducible** when it has no nontrivial invariant subspaces in the representation used in the paper. **Conjecture on extremal automata.** Every extremal synchronizing automaton is irreducible.

The conjecture would extend the known relationship between extremal synchronizing automata and irreducibility beyond the examples currently available. The source notes that every known extremal automaton is irreducible, but does not establish the assertion in general.

371607.title: Rank-two word conjecture for irreducible automata
371607.statement:
Let $\mathcal{A}=(Q,\Sigma,\delta)$ be an irreducible automaton. For a word $u\in\Sigma^*$, let $\operatorname{rk}(u)$ denote the cardinality of the image of $Q$ under $u$. **Rank-two word conjecture.** There exists a word $u\in\Sigma^*$ such that

$$
\operatorname{rk}(u)=2.
$$

All irreducible examples constructed in the paper have former-rank two, which motivates the conjecture. The source presents it as unresolved and notes that simple, non-irreducible automata of former-rank two also exist, so rank two alone cannot characterize irreducibility.

371619.title: Exact star-colored Turán bound conjecture
371619.statement:
For integers $r$ and $s\geq r-1$, let $G_1,\ldots,G_s\subseteq\binom{[n]}{2}$ be graphs whose edges are $(r-1)$-star edge-colored and whose underlying graphs are $K_r$-free. Here $e(G_i)$ denotes the number of edges of $G_i$, and $t(n,r-1)$ denotes the Turán number of $K_r$ on $n$ vertices. **Exact star-colored Turán bound conjecture.**

$$
\sum_{i=1}^{s}e(G_i)\leq s\cdot t(n,r-1).
$$

The preceding theorem establishes the same bound only up to an additive term $sn$ in the regime $s\geq r-1$; removing that error term would give the exact extremal value in the corresponding application. The source leaves this conjecture open.
